findings.title: I9: gitleaks corpus recall is 6% (7 of 152 testable rules fully masked)
findings.claim: exists secret s matching a gitleaks default rule with maskSecrets(embed(s)) containing s. Measured over fc.stringMatching samples of 152 of the 222 rules (70 not regex-generatable), 15000 samples: full-match recall 6.4%; 100 vendor-keyed rules (airtable, algolia, asana, ...) 0.0%; 52 prefix rules 18.9%; only 7 of 152 rules fully masked (github-pat/oauth/refresh/app/fine-grained, slack-bot, slack-legacy-bot)

findings.observed: gen.mts: plain recall 0.064, keyed 0.000, prefixed 0.189, 136 rules with zero recall. Curated 80-case table: 63 leak (recall 21%); the 15 control formats pass.
findings.fix: Replace the 9 hand patterns with the gitleaks rule set (or keyword+entropy detector) compiled to JS; add a corpus recall gate in CI.

findings.title: I9: camelCase / compound key names (clientSecret, authToken, AccountKey, dbPassword, privateKey) bypass CREDENTIAL
findings.claim: CREDENTIAL needs a word boundary then [_-]-separated prefixes, so a keyword in the middle of a camelCase identifier is never anchored; "key", "credentials", "private_key", sessionid, DB_PASS, accessToken in JSON are not matched either
findings.witness: cd E:\Dev\cws-claude && node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/findings/redaction-recall.test.ts --test-name-pattern "camelCase|AccountKey|privateKey|secretKey|dbPassword|DB_PASS|bearerToken|accessToken|credentials"
findings.observed: maskSecrets of clientSecret: "<32 chars>" and {"accessToken":"..."} returned unchanged.
findings.fix: Match keywords as substrings of the identifier ([A-Za-z0-9_.-]*(secret|token|password|passwd|pwd|credential|private[_-]?key|api[_-]?key|account[_-]?key)[A-Za-z0-9_.-]*) and drop the leading word boundary.

findings.title: I9: passwords with spaces, in prose, short, or given as CLI args survive
findings.claim: value class is [^\s"',;]{4,} and the key must be followed by : or =. So password = "correct horse battery staple" only loses the first word, "the password is X", password=abc, curl -u user:pass, cli --token X, Cookie sessionid=, ?key=, X-Amz-Signature= leak
findings.witness: cd E:\Dev\cws-claude && node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/findings/redaction-recall.test.ts --test-name-pattern "quoted password|yaml password|short password|password in prose|--token|--api-key|curl -u|Cookie|url \?key"
findings.observed: redactSecrets output contains the password words / token verbatim.
findings.fix: Quoted values: match up to the closing quote; accept length >=1; add --flag value, -u user:pass, Cookie/Set-Cookie, signature query params.

findings.title: I9: truncated or non-RSA PEM blocks (no END marker, PGP) leak the key body
findings.claim: PEM regex needs the full BEGIN..END pair: a block cut by a limit, pager or log line, a PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK, or a JSON private_key without END keeps the base64 body
findings.witness: cd E:\Dev\cws-claude && node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/findings/redaction-recall.test.ts --test-name-pattern "PEM truncated|PGP private|service-account json"
findings.observed: "-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY----- C48m6G..." survives redactSecrets.
findings.fix: Mask from BEGIN..PRIVATE KEY to END or to end-of-text; handle PRIVATE KEY BLOCK.

findings.title: I9: URL / connection-string secrets: empty user, @ in password, Azure AccountKey and SAS sig leak
findings.claim: URL_PASSWORD requires a non-empty user and a password without @ (stops at first @): postgres://:pw@h leaks, postgres://u:pa@ss@h leaks "ss"; AccountKey=<base64> and sig=<43> are not matched
findings.witness: cd E:\Dev\cws-claude && node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/findings/redaction-recall.test.ts --test-name-pattern "postgres|azure|presigned"
findings.observed: redactSecrets keeps the password / key tail.
findings.fix: Allow empty user, take the password up to the last @ before the host, add Azure patterns.

findings.title: I9: dump / claim add / evidence add persist pasted secrets verbatim in .cws/events.jsonl
findings.claim: for every free text t entered via dump, claim add, evidence add: events.jsonl contains t unmasked. Masking happens only when a context pack is rendered, so the log, backups, sync payloads and every non-prompt view hold the raw secret

findings.title: I9: shorten() in warnings.ts does not redact; cws status prints stored secrets
findings.claim: shorten(text) only collapses whitespace and truncates; quoteList() puts it into Warning.message, which cws status prints and the pack Warnings section embeds
findings.witness: cd E:\Dev\cws-claude && node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/findings/stored-secrets.test.ts --test-name-pattern "shorten|cws status"
findings.observed: `cws status` output contains the ghp_ token inside the UNCONFIRMED_AI_CLAIMS warning.
findings.fix: Apply maskSecrets inside shorten() (or quoteList).

findings.title: DoS: maskSecrets is quadratic on hyphenated text; 20 KB notes make cws context take 15 s
findings.claim: time(maskSecrets("a-" x n)) is Theta(n^2): CREDENTIAL starts a scan at every word boundary and walks (?:[A-Za-z0-9]+[_-])* to the end; the PEM pattern is also quadratic on repeated BEGIN headers without END. redactSecrets masks BEFORE truncating, so an SARIF message up to the 10 MB cap is fully scanned; any stored note or claim (max 20000 chars) hits it on every render
findings.witness: cd E:\Dev\cws-claude && node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/findings/stored-secrets.test.ts --test-name-pattern "linear"
findings.observed: maskSecrets 60 KB: 12468 ms; 10 stored 20 KB notes: `cws context explore` 14846 ms; 60 KB SARIF message: ingest 12761 ms; 432 KB of BEGIN headers: 5187 ms.
findings.fix: Truncate to the limit before masking (cap at ~8 KB), and rewrite CREDENTIAL without the nested quantifier.

findings.title: Over-redaction: rule id like "hardcoded-password:" eats the first word of the finding message

findings.witness: cd E:\Dev\cws-claude && node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/findings/stored-secrets.test.ts --test-name-pattern "rule id looks like a key"
findings.observed: cws-finding:... [high] semgrep hardcoded-password: [redacted] credentials found in config (a.ts); same for gitleaks generic-api-key.
findings.fix: Redact message and snippet separately before composing the title; do not run CREDENTIAL over rule ids.

findings.title: I11: untrusted-data boundary is static and U+2028/U+0085 are not escaped in the pack
findings.claim: The fence and the closing notice are fixed strings (no per-run nonce) and JSON.stringify leaves U+2028/2029/0085 raw, so stored text can carry line separators that some renderers or models treat as newline + fence + fake heading. With plain \n the fence and headings CANNOT be forged (each record is one JSON line); that part holds
findings.witness: cd E:\Dev\cws-claude && node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/findings/prompt-injection.test.ts --test-name-pattern "exotic line|unguessable"
findings.observed: the pack contains raw U+2028 from a claim; two renders of one state use identical delimiters.
findings.fix: Escape U+2028/2029/0085 in dataLine; add a random boundary token to the fence and the closing notice (OWASP LLM01).

findings.title: upsertBlock leaves a stale cws block when END was removed or the markers are quoted elsewhere
findings.claim: upsertBlock uses lastIndexOf(BEGIN): if the real block lost its END a second block is appended and the stale protocol stays; if a later line quotes the markers, that quote is replaced and the real block stays stale; agents then read two conflicting protocols
findings.witness: cd E:\Dev\cws-claude && node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/findings/agents-install.test.ts
findings.observed: two BEGIN markers after upsert on a damaged file; old block text survives when a docs line quotes the markers.
findings.fix: Find a matched BEGIN..END pair; if BEGIN has no END replace to end of file or refuse.

findings.title: findings ingest buffers all of stdin before checking the 10 MB cap
findings.claim: readStdin() concatenates all of stdin, then readInput compares raw.length with MAX_INPUT_CHARS; files are allowed up to 40 MB (MAX*4) before the char check; no streaming limit
